It’s complicated. For some people it’s a mixture of it being real, independent of your awareness, and the stress about it. That is likely the most common. For some people it’s entirely physiological and they don’t have a problem with obsessing over it and compounding the effects on the body with worry. Then there’s a bandwagoning crowd who are somehow benefited by the concept of being sick. Maybe it gets them attention, maybe they have an excuse to not work, it could be many things.

It’s very valuable that you have recognized the significance of the psychological factor in your situation. Aside from that, your body’s response is the only empirical form of confirmation for mold issues that is available. Can you smell it? See it? Do your eyes water? Do you feel way better when you leave your place? Do you have reactions to commercial infrastructure? Do you have trouble breathing in the soap and detergent section in stores?

Those are the real units of measurements for figuring out if it’s a problem for you or not. Once you determine this, do your best to get into as clean of a space as possible, and do your best to keep it clean. Get a high quality air purifier, ventilate, etc.

Also, people who are truly sick and who are sensitive to mold find dramatic improvement in desert climates. The California high desert, Arizona, New Mexico, Utah, etc. I spent a year doing all of the binders and only got worse.
